# How work is done here

This project uses **CooperativeAICoding**: people answer plain-English briefs,
an AI translates them into specs, and a person approves every plan before any
code is written. Nothing here depends on one vendor's model or tool.

**This is the starter, not this project's rules.** The sections below marked
*not yet filled in* are waiting on the brief. The procedures and the working
agreement are true from the first day.

## The procedures

One file per thing you may be asked to do. Read the file and follow it exactly.

| When the request is | Follow |
|---|---|
| fill a brief in from an existing codebase | `ai-only/procedures/draft.md` |
| turn a filled-in brief into a spec | `ai-only/procedures/translate.md` |
| add a new page, endpoint or database model | `ai-only/procedures/new-item.md` |
| build the next iteration of an approved spec | `ai-only/procedures/build.md` |
| set up a solution's pipeline and infrastructure | `ai-only/procedures/pipeline.md` |
| write these rules out for another AI tool | `ai-only/procedures/emit-guardrails.md` |

These are plain Markdown and vendor-neutral. In Claude Code they are also
reachable as `/draft`, `/translate`, `/new-item`, `/build`, `/pipeline` and
`/emit-guardrails`; with any other agent, read the file.

## Where things are

| Path | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `Project_brief.md` | The whole-project brief. People write it; you never author it. |
| `<solution>/<item>.md|.json` | One brief per page, endpoint or database model. |
| `ai-only/` | Your workspace: the specs, the plans, the round reports, the code map. |
| `ai-only/Project_system.md` | The System Spec and the **Project Digest** — read the Digest, not the whole spec. *Does not exist yet: created by `translate.md`.* |
| `ai-only/Code_map.md` | The reuse index: what already exists, so it is not rebuilt. *Does not exist yet: created by `build.md`.* |
| `tools/` | The three checks. Run them; they are not advisory. |

A row marked *does not exist yet* is an output, not somewhere to look today.

## House rules

**Not yet filled in.** They come from the Project Brief's coding-standards
answers. Until `/translate` has run, follow the working agreement below and ask
rather than assume.

## Security

**Not yet filled in.** One rule applies regardless: **secret values are never
written into code, config, logs or documents.** Reference them by name.

## Testing

**Not yet filled in.** Until the brief states a level of cover, write a failing
test first, then just enough code to pass it, and say in your round record what
you did not test. Do not invent a threshold.

## What we are working towards

**Not yet filled in.** The Project Brief names deliverables in order, each with
what makes it done. Until it does, there is no stopping point — so keep changes
small, finish what is asked, and do not start adjacent work on the assumption it
is next.

## The working agreement

- Build the **smallest thing** that answers the request. No unrequested extras.
- Treat existing code as **working in production**, even if it looks broken.
- **Never invent scope.** Anything the brief does not say is an open question,
  not a decision you get to make.
- **Reuse before building.** Check the code map for something that already does
  the job before writing anything new, and add a row for whatever you build. It
  lives at `ai-only/Code_map.md` and *does not exist yet* — the first build
  creates it from `ai-only/3-code-map.template.md`.
- **When you cannot understand something, stop and say so.** A guess that becomes
  code is the failure this whole way of working exists to prevent. Saying "I do
  not know how you want this done" is the most useful thing you can write, not an
  admission of failure.
- A person reviews and approves a plan before code is written.

## When you finish, write this down

Append to `ROUND-RECORD.md`, one heading each:

### What I did
### What I could not do  (and what you would need to tell me)
### Debt I left behind  (one paragraph each, so each can become its own work item)

Debt that is not written down is debt that gets paid by surprise.
`node tools/round-record-lint.mjs` checks the record exists and answers all
three, because this is the one rule that rests entirely on you remembering.

## The checks

```bash
node tools/brief-lint.mjs         every item names a deliverable the brief lists
node tools/code-map-lint.mjs      the code map matches the code, and surfaces are explained
node tools/round-record-lint.mjs  a round record exists and answers all three questions
```

## What this file cannot give you

These are the rules and the procedures, not the machinery. **Nothing here can
make you follow them.** A procedure is a document you are pointed at; whether
you read it is not checked. Model and effort per item, what a run cost,
deny-by-default policy and a bounded place to run commands live in the
CoperativeAI desktop app.

The part that does not depend on which model turned up is the approval gate: a
person reads the plan before code is written. Keep that one.
